newsitem.title: GREECE: CALCULATION RULES ON GREEK CPI-INDEXED BONDS.
newsitem.headline: CALCULATION RULES ON GREEK CPI-INDEXED BONDS.

text.p: The following formulas on
CPI-indexed bonds were made available by the finance ministry:
Let K= redemption amount
N= nominal amount
C= coupon payment amount
r= annual real interest rate
K= N* (reference CPI index at maturity / reference CPI at
issue date)
C= r* Nominal value* (reference index at coupon payment
date/reference CPI at issue date)
If the settlement date is the first of a month, the
reference CPI index is the CPI falling threee calendar months
earlier.
If the settlement date is a day other than the first of the
month, the reference CPI index is found by linear interpolation
between the CPI falling two and three months earlier.
Example: 5-year, 4.0pct CPI-indexed bond issued on May 19,
Issue date = May 19, 1997
Maturity date = May 19, 2002
CPI (issue date)= CPI(February)+ (18/30)*
(CPI(March)-CPI(February)
Market conventions for interest payments are a 360-day year
and a 30-day month and the CPI index is rounded off to one
decimal, the ministry said.
Coupon stripping would be allowed from issue day and
investrors are guaranteed the nominal value in case of
deflation, it said.
Greece is going to issue 4.0 percent, five- and 10-year
coupon CPI-indexed bonds on May 19. A finance ministry offical
told Reuters that gross selling commissions for five- and
10-year CPI-indexed bonds would be 0.95 percent and 1.10
percent.
--Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
